cards.front: Recall a key point about Retrieval & Literal Comprehension
cards.back: Retrieval means finding information that is directly stated in the text. You don't need to guess or interpret - the answer is right there in black and white.

cards.front: Recall a key point about Retrieval & Literal Comprehension
cards.back: Top Tips: Write in your own words where possible (but keep close to the text) You can use bullet points or numbered lists Each point should be a complete idea Don't repeat the same point in different words

cards.front: What should you know about examiner's tip?
cards.back: This is one of the easiest questions on the paper. Don't overthink it - just find four things and write them down. Aim to complete this in about 5 minutes.

cards.front: What should you know about retrieval exam strategy?
cards.back: This is the easiest question on the paper - don't overcomplicate it. For AQA Paper 1 Q1 (4 marks), spend no more than 5 minutes. Read the question carefully, note any line references, scan for keywords, then write four clear points. For AQA Paper 2 Q1 (true/false), go back to the text and verify each option before choosing. Examiners mark this question generously - they want to give you full marks. Just find the information and state it clearly.

cards.front: What does Using inference when retrieval is asked for mean?
cards.back: You're guessing instead of finding what's stated (e.g. Find the exact information in the text)

cards.front: What does Quoting too much mean?
cards.back: You lose marks for copying whole sections (e.g. Select only the relevant words)

cards.front: What does Not answering all parts of the question mean?
cards.back: You might miss easy marks (e.g. Check you've listed the right number of points)

cards.front: What does Repeating the same point mean?
cards.back: You won't get marks for saying the same thing twice (e.g. Make each point different)

cards.front: What does Analysing language when asked to retrieve mean?
cards.back: That's a different question type (e.g. Just find and state the facts)
These questions ask you to list specific details from a text. They're worth 4 marks - 1 mark for each correct point.
Circle the correct option - the answer is directly stated in the text.
Summarise the differences or similarities between two texts.
Quickly move your eyes over the text to locate specific keywords related to the question.
Read quickly to get the gist of each paragraph before looking for specific details.
If the question gives line numbers, read those lines carefully first.
